title: List, Set, Queue and Map
context: What are the differences between List, Set, Queue and Map?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A List is an ordered collection that allows duplicates and access by index, such as ArrayList. A Set holds unique elements with no index, such as HashSet, TreeSet or LinkedHashSet. A Queue holds elements for processing in order, usually first in first out, such as ArrayDeque or LinkedList. A Map stores key-value pairs with unique keys, such as HashMap. Map is not a subtype of Collection, though its views are collections.

points.title: Duplicates and order
points.why: List keeps order and duplicates, Set removes duplicates, and each has its own ordering rules.

points.title: Map is separate
points.why: A Map is not a Collection. Its key set and values are views of the map.
